Bluetongue: latest situation

Overview of current bluetongue cases, risk level, vaccinations and restrictions.

From:
Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs and Animal and Plant Health Agency
Published:
31 July 2026
Last updated:
30 August 2026 — See all updates

Be vigilant for signs of bluetongue and report it if you suspect it.

Total number of confirmed cases (premises)

There have been 722 cases of bluetongue serotype 3 (BTV-3) in the UK in the 2026 to 2027 bluetongue season. A case is defined as a premises on which at least one bluetongue positive animal has been confirmed. This includes:

  • 637 cases in England
  • 68 cases in Wales
  • 17 cases in Scotland
  • 0 cases in Northern Ireland

There have been no cases of bluetongue serotype 8 (BTV-8) in the 2026 to 2027 bluetongue season.

Where animals with suspect clinical signs are reported, Defra funds the cost of diagnostic testing for up to 3 affected animals.

The bluetongue case map shows the location of all premises in Great Britain where one or more animals have tested positive by PCR for bluetongue.

There are currently 2,546 potential cases of bluetongue under investigation in Great Britain. These are premises that have reported suspicious clinical signs and are under investigation.

Wellbeing support for animal keepers

See our list of organisations offering wellbeing support to those in the farming community.

Risk level

The risk of bluetongue virus incursion from:

  • all routes – is medium (occurs regularly)
  • airborne routes – is low (event is rare, but could occur)

This includes serotypes that are not currently circulating in England.

The midges that spread bluetongue became active again on 31 March 2026.

Temperatures are consistently high enough in parts of the UK and nearby continental Europe for the virus to develop inside the midges. This means onward transmission is now occurring and there is increased risk of transmission from midges blown across the Channel. Animals can also get infected through germinal products (semen, ova or embryos).

Control zones

There are bluetongue restricted zones across the whole of England and Wales.

You can check the restricted zones using the bluetongue zone map.

England: country-wide restricted zone

The whole of England is in a bluetongue restricted zone. You can move animals within England without a specific bluetongue licence or pre-movement testing.

You need a specific licence to freeze germinal products (semen, ova and embryo) anywhere in England and testing is required. Keepers are responsible for the cost of sampling, postage and testing. There is more detail in the declaration.

Read the details of the restricted zone in England.

Wales: country-wide restricted zone

An all-Wales restricted zone was introduced on 10 November 2025. This has the following effects:

  • free movement of livestock – livestock movements between England and Wales do not require bluetongue vaccination or mitigation measures
  • restrictions on germinal products – you must test donor animals before freezing and marketing germinal products, as this provides quality assurance and reduces the risk of longer-term bluetongue transmission

Scotland: temporary control zone (TCZ)

A temporary control zone (TCZ) was put in place in South West Scotland on 20 August 2026.

Livestock keepers must follow the movement controls on animals and germinal products and apply for a licence where needed. Check the bluetongue case map and GOV.SCOT for more information.

Moving live animals from a restricted zone (RZ) to Scotland (including shows, markets, gatherings, even if temporary)

England, Wales, Northern Ireland and the Isle of Man all have bluetongue virus BTV RZs, and any movement of bluetongue susceptible animals from a BTV RZ to Scotland must comply with the conditions set out in the general movement licence EXD608(EW). These controls came into force on 1 June 2026 and will remain in force until at least 9 September 2026. Check the rules on movements to and from Scotland.

Defra’s bluetongue control strategy

Defra controls cases of bluetongue by following the Bluetongue: disease control framework in England.

Historical cases

The first cases of bluetongue virus serotype 3 (BTV-3) of the 2026 to 2027 outbreak season was confirmed on 10 July 2026.

2025 to 2026 outbreak season (1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026)

There were 348 cases of bluetongue in Great Britain in the 2025 to 2026 bluetongue season. In:

  • England, there were 324 cases of bluetongue – including 311 cases of only BTV-3, 5 cases of only BTV-8, 7 cases with both BTV-3 and BTV-8 and 1 case of BTV (serotype unknown)
  • Wales, there have been 24 cases of BTV-3
  • There were no cases in Scotland

These cases were confirmed between 11 July 2025 and 23 June 2026.

There were 5 confirmed cases of BTV-3 in Northern Ireland.

2024 to 2025 outbreak season (1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025)

Defra confirmed 160 BTV-3 cases in England and 2 from high risk moves in Wales. One case of bluetongue virus serotype 12 (BTV-12) was confirmed in England on 7 February 2025 Giving a total of 163 cases.

These cases were confirmed between 26 August 2024 and 31 May 2025.

2023 to 2024 outbreak season (1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025)

Between 10 November 2023 and 3 March 2024 Defra confirmed 126 BTV-3 cases in England on 73 premises (119 cattle and 7 sheep). These BTV-3 cases were the first UK BTV incursions for over 15 years. 

Prior to these cases the last confirmed outbreak of bluetongue was an outbreak of bluetongue virus serotype 8 (BTV-8), which took place over 2007 to 2008.
